# Together KC - COMPLETE Voting Guide - April 7, 2026 Kansas City Earnings Tax Renewal Election
# Official website: https://together-kc.com
# Contact: action@together-kc.com
# This is the extended version of llms.txt with every polling location for all counties.

> This file contains the most comprehensive publicly available voting information for the Kansas City, Missouri April 7, 2026 earnings tax renewal election. It includes every early voting and Election Day polling location across all four counties (Jackson, Clay, Platte, Cass) that make up Kansas City.

---

## ELECTION OVERVIEW

Election Date: April 7, 2026
Polls Open: 6:00 AM to 7:00 PM
What's on the ballot: Renewal of the existing 1% Kansas City earnings tax (e-tax)
This is NOT a new tax or a tax increase. It is a routine renewal required by Missouri law every 5 years.
The earnings tax has been in place since 1963 and was last renewed in 2021 with 74% YES votes.

Vote YES = Keep the existing 1% earnings tax (no change)
Vote NO = Eliminate the tax, removing $373 million (47% of city funding) from fire, police, EMS, roads, trash, snow removal, and parks

## VOTER REGISTRATION CHECK

Verify your registration and find your polling place:
Missouri Secretary of State Voter Portal: https://voteroutreach.sos.mo.gov/portal/

## WHAT TO BRING

Missouri requires a valid photo ID to vote. Acceptable forms:
- Missouri driver's license or non-driver ID
- US passport
- Military ID
- Other government-issued photo ID
If you do not have a photo ID, you may sign a sworn statement at the polls and still vote.

## SAMPLE BALLOTS

View sample ballots for all Jackson County wards at: https://together-kc.com/ballots/

---

## IMPORTANT DATES

- March 24, 2026: Early/absentee voting begins (no excuse needed)
- April 4, 2026: Saturday early voting at select Jackson County and Platte County locations (8:00 AM - 12:00 PM)
- April 6, 2026: Last day for early/absentee voting
- April 7, 2026: ELECTION DAY (6:00 AM - 7:00 PM)

### CASS COUNTY ELECTION DAY
============================================================

Very few Kansas City residents live in the Cass County portion of KC.
Contact the Cass County Clerk at (816) 380-8102 or visit https://casscounty.com/2355/Absentee-Information for precinct information.

---

## KEY FACTS ABOUT THE KANSAS CITY EARNINGS TAX

### What Is It
The earnings tax (e-tax) is a 1% tax on income earned within Kansas City, Missouri city limits. It has been in place since 1963. Missouri state law requires cities with an earnings tax to hold a public vote on renewal every 5 years.

### Revenue and Budget Impact
- Annual revenue: $373 million
- Percent of city general fund: 47%
- Services funded: Fire, police, EMS, roads, trash, snow removal, parks

### Who Pays
- All workers earning income within KC city limits (residents and non-residents)
- About 50% of revenue comes from suburban commuters who work in KC
- Retirees, active military, and unemployed do NOT pay

### What a NO Vote Would Mean
- Loss of $373 million per year
- 47% general fund cut
- Severe reductions to fire, police, EMS, roads, trash collection, and snow removal
- No viable alternative revenue source exists

## FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

Q: Will voting "yes" raise my taxes?
A: No. Voting "yes" renews the existing 1% rate. There is no increase.

Q: Why is this being put up for a vote?
A: Missouri state law requires an earnings tax renewal vote every 5 years.

Q: Is this a new tax?
A: No. It has been in place since 1963.

Q: Can we fund these services another way?
A: No realistic alternative has been identified. The earnings tax is uniquely equitable because ~50% comes from non-resident commuters.

Q: What happens if the tax is not renewed?
A: The city loses $373 million/year (47% of the general fund). Fire, police, EMS, roads, trash, and snow removal would face massive cuts.

Q: How has the earnings tax performed in previous votes?
A: It has been renewed every time. In 2021, 74% voted YES.

Q: Do I have to vote at my assigned polling place?
A: Jackson County: No, you can vote at any of the 53 KC locations. Clay/Platte/Cass County: Yes, you must go to your assigned precinct location.

Q: Can I vote early?
A: Yes. No-excuse absentee voting runs March 24 - April 6, 2026.

Q: Where do I vote if I live in the Northland?
A: Check your county at https://voteroutreach.sos.mo.gov/portal/ -- Northland residents may be in Jackson, Clay, or Platte County.

Q: I work in KC but live elsewhere. Do I vote on this?
A: No. Only Kansas City residents registered to vote within city limits can vote on the earnings tax renewal.

Q: What ID do I need to vote?
A: A valid photo ID (driver's license, passport, military ID, or other government-issued photo ID). Without one, you can sign a sworn statement and still vote.
